meta.name: The Crude Oracle $10,000,000 Quantitative Paper Fund
meta.description: Institutional-style simulated portfolio. Prices are delayed or indicative public marks frozen at the decision timestamp. The July 2026 $1,000,000 sample book is archived unchanged at data/archive/virtual-portfolio-1m-2026-07.json and is not part of this NAV.
meta.objective: Determine whether The Crude Oracle's combined energy, shipping, macroeconomic, geopolitical, quantitative and AI intelligence can generate persistent positive risk-adjusted returns from a simulated $10,000,000 portfolio.
meta.disclaimer: This is a virtual paper-trading record for education and platform demonstration only. No real capital is deployed. It is not financial advice, investment advice, trading advice or a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any security, commodity, derivative, ETF, fund or financial product. Trading and investing involve risk, including loss of capital. Past performance and simulated performance do not guarantee future results. Users must conduct their own research and consult a regulated financial adviser where appropriate.

account.oracle_confidence_note: The index is the exposure-weighted confidence of open positions. With no open risk it is not printed as a market view.
account.largest_risk: No open position. The predefined risk in the book is $0. Opportunity cost of holding cash is not a stop-loss.

position_limits: Core position: maximum 15% of NAV, measured as notional exposure
High-conviction position: maximum 20% of NAV — written justification required
Gross notional of a spread counts both legs; the stop is on the spread, not on each leg alone
rules.cash_reserve: Cash is a residual, not a target to be filled. Capital stays in cash when no idea clears the confidence gate.
rules.risk_per_trade: Normal trade risk is 0.25%–1.0% of NAV. An exceptional multi-factor case may risk up to 1.5% of NAV. Capital allocated is not capital at risk. A stop is a plan, not a guarantee against a gap.
rules.confidence_gate: 90–100 exceptional. 80–89 very strong. 70–79 normal size. 60–69 reduced size. Below 60 watchlist only.
conduct: No rewritten entries after the market moves
Winning and losing trades stay in the archive
A quiet week is a valid decision

allocation.note: Top-ranked idea stayed on the watchlist. Confidence 50.

trade_log.thesis: Six independent ideas were ranked from public marks frozen at 11:21 UTC on 5 October 2026. The best, a short Brent–WTI spread, scored 50. The trade gate is 60. Nothing was opened.
trade_log.catalyst: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report on 7 October 2026, and a full-session settlement of the Brent–WTI spread, are the next facts that can change the ranking.
trade_log.supporting_data: See weekly report 2026-W41. Internal Oracle shipping, curve, positioning, balance and hypothesis files are the 15 July 2026 sample set and were excluded.
trade_log.risk: The risk of this decision is opportunity cost if the war premium collapses without the fund. That cost is not booked as a loss, and it is not a reason to invent a position.
trade_log.invalidation: A later week may trade the spread if confidence reaches 60 with a predefined stop still inside 1.0% of NAV. This record is not revised if that happens.
trade_log.holding_period: Cash through the 7 October EIA print. Next formal cycle is week 42.
trade_log.confidence: 50 on the best idea — below the trade gate
sources: Yahoo Finance futures marks, 5 October 2026, 11:21 UTC
The Economic Times, 5 October 2026, oil price note citing a Reuters shipping tally
Secondary compilations of EIA weekly commercial crude stocks through the week ending 25 September 2026
trade_log.strategy_fit: The fund is allowed to hold cash. Activity is not a substitute for a cleared signal.
trade_log.why_it_could_be_wrong: The war premium in Brent can compress before the next committee, and the cash book will not participate. That miss, if it happens, is recorded in the next weekly report. It is not backfilled into this one.

equity_curve.note: Inception. Cash. No paper trade opened.

marks.source: Yahoo Finance futures chart, regularMarketPrice. Delayed and indicative, not a settlement and not a licensed real-time feed.
marks.rbob_note: Excluded from every score. The printed last was below the printed session low, and Monday volume was a small fraction of the prior three sessions.
marks.spread_window: 127 daily closes, 6 April 2026 to 5 October 2026. Median spread $5.16. High $13.21 on 29 September. Since the 23 September break the spread has traded $9.44 to $13.21. The decision spread of $12.18 sits inside that war-regime range.

opportunities.structure: Long WTI Nov 26, short Brent, equal barrels
opportunities.target_label: Spread $6.50, still above the six-month median of $5.16
opportunities.summary: The spread is wide against the last six months and only ordinary inside the post-23 September range. Exports, an OSP cut and a planned G7 stock release lean toward compression. A live war leans the other way. Score 50. Not opened.

factors.note: About the 98th percentile of 127 sessions against a $5.16 median, but inside the $9.44–$13.21 range that has held since 23 September. Not a fresh extreme of the current regime.

US commercial crude built +2.97 mb (week of 18 Sep) and +0.92 mb (week of 25 Sep) to about 427.3 mb in secondary EIA compilations. Aramco cut November official prices to Asia to six-year lows. Middle East exports were reported above pre-war levels on four of seven days in the last week of September.
ICE dollar index 102.254 versus a prior close of 101.45. A firmer dollar leans against flat-price crude. It says little about the spread itself.
The trade needs the war premium to narrow. The Iran war, reported attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, and an unconfirmed Houthi claim of strikes on Aramco sites all point the other way.
Heating-oil crack still about $102, so the product premium has not collapsed. Settled gasoline cracks on 1–2 October were off the 30 September peak. Today's RBOB tick was discarded.

Oracle shipping, curve, positioning and balance files are the 15 July sample and were not used. Brent in the Economic Times note earlier on 5 October was $101.60, versus $102.33 on the later futures mark.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: Hormuz disruption can widen Brent against WTI through any stop. The six-month percentile also mixes the pre-war market with the war market, so the spread can look 'extreme' while simply being the new price of the conflict.
opportunities.invalidation: A settlement above $13.21, a confirmed sustained halt of Middle East exports, or a fresh EIA crude draw large enough to make WTI the scarce barrel.

opportunities.structure: Short HO Nov 26 against long WTI Nov 26
opportunities.target_label: Crack $75, still far above early July
opportunities.summary: The distillate crack is extremely wide versus July and has been stuck near $100–$118 for two weeks. Fading it is a bet that the war premium in diesel eases. Monday HO volume was too thin to treat the tick as a break.

factors.note: HO Nov was $3.30 on 6 July and $4.57 on the decision mark. The crack has held roughly $98–$118 since 24 September, so this is a regime, not a one-day spike.
No October refinery-run figure was available. A crack this wide can be the physical result of lost distillate supply rather than a mispricing.
The dollar is not the driver of a $100 crack.
Diesel and jet are the products most exposed to a Gulf infrastructure shock. Geopolitics opposes a short crack.
Settled RBOB cracks eased from about $54 on 30 September to about $48 on 2 October. That is partial confirmation, not a collapse.
Monday HO volume was about 5,000 contracts against roughly 52,000 on each of the prior three sessions. The RBOB print was unusable.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: A refinery outage or a halt in distillate loadings can push the crack through $120 before a stop is tradable.
opportunities.invalidation: A full-session HO settlement that takes the crack above $118, or a confirmed loss of a major distillate export stream.

opportunities.target_label: $94, a partial give-back of the war premium
opportunities.summary: Supply additions are real. A naked short into an active war does not pay for the stop the risk manager would require. Reward to $94 is smaller than risk to $112.

factors.note: Brent is below the 24 September high of $106.60 and is not a breakdown. No term structure was available, so backwardation or contango is unknown.

G7 governments have plans to release stocks, the size of which was not stated in the article used. Exports recovered on several late-September days. OSPs to Asia were cut. US crude stocks built into 25 September.
A firmer dollar is a mild headwind for flat-price crude.
Shorting Brent is shorting the instrument that reprices Hormuz first. The Economic Times quoted JPMorgan: the endgame is not something the street knows how to model.
Products are off the 30 September extremes and the distillate crack is still near $102. The complex has not stood down.
Early-session futures mark. Internal curve module excluded as stale sample data. EIA's own site returned an error during this session, so stock levels are secondary compilations.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: One credible infrastructure headline can gap Brent through $112. The stop is a plan, not a cap on loss.
opportunities.invalidation: Already fails the gate on risk/reward. A trade would also be invalidated by a confirmed export collapse through Hormuz.

opportunities.summary: The war is the bull case. US stock builds, cheaper Asian official prices and a firmer dollar are the bear case. Geopolitics alone does not clear the gate.

factors.note: $90.15 is inside the post-break range. The Monday low was already $89.31, so a tight stop is noise and a wide stop ruins the ratio.
Two consecutive US crude builds and an Aramco OSP cut oppose a new long.
Firmer dollar.
An active Iran war and Hormuz risk are the reason a long WTI scores higher here than the shorts. The risk is already in the price.
WTI is the lagging leg of a $12 spread. Owning it outright also takes the war premium without being paid the spread dislocation.
Same stale internal modules. WTI volume on the Monday mark was usable; the rest of the complex was not fully settled.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: The premium can come out faster than the war ends, particularly if the G7 release and the export recovery continue together.
opportunities.invalidation: A weekly EIA build combined with Brent losing the $100 handle would remove the reason to be long the lagging leg.

opportunities.holding_period: Into the first winter storage prints, had it been opened
opportunities.summary: A 2:1 illustration is not a signal. November gas is inside a $2.91–$3.16 band. No October storage number was in the decision set. Calendar seasonality was not treated as evidence.

factors.note: $3.03 is not a dislocation. The three-month range is tight and the Monday change was a cent.
No fresh US gas storage figure was used. LNG feedgas and a winter path were not verified this session.
No power-demand or weather anomaly was established.
US gas has not repriced with the oil war. That supports independence from the crude book. It does not support a long.
Crude is in a war regime and Henry Hub is not. There is no confirmed spillover to trade.
The futures mark is clean. The inventory side is missing, so the family cannot score higher.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: A storage surprise or an early cold shot can still lift November gas. The fund will have missed it because the evidence was not in hand.
opportunities.invalidation: A verified storage deficit versus the five-year average, or a feedgas surge, would reopen the idea. Neither was in this file.

opportunities.structure: Long a broad energy equity basket
opportunities.entry_label: No decision mark. US cash equities were not in session at 11:21 UTC.
opportunities.summary: XLE's last Yahoo print was the prior cash close at $62.82. A paper equity trade was not priced off a closed market.

factors.note: One stale cash print is not a trend, a reversal or a spread.
Equities would express the same unresolved crude argument at a lag, with company-level noise added.
A firmer dollar and an unresolved war are not a clean equity setup.
Producers can benefit if the premium holds. That is already the unresolved flat-price question.
Crude futures were live. The equity market was not. They cannot be combined into one timestamped trade.
No cash-session mark at the decision time. Score capped almost at zero for that reason.

opportunities.why_it_could_be_wrong: Energy equities can re-rate on the open while this book is in cash. That is accepted.
opportunities.invalidation: Revisit only on a same-day cash print, and only if the crude decision itself has cleared the gate. Equities are not a way around a weak crude signal.

weekly_reports.title: Week 41 — inception
weekly_reports.loss_analysis: There is no losing trade to analyse. The committee's error, if it made one, will show up later as a missed move, and that miss will be written here in a later week without editing this report.
weekly_reports.what_worked: Nothing has been proven. The process held: conflicting news was separated from a tradable mark, the RBOB print was thrown out, and a wide spread was not promoted into a trade just because the fund was new.
weekly_reports.process_review: Signal families that were missing — live shipping, the forward curve, positioning and open interest — capped data quality and stopped every idea below 60. The 7 October EIA release is the next primary fundamental. A full-session Brent and WTI settlement is the next structure check. Internal Oracle modules dated 15 July 2026 stay excluded until they are refreshed with dated, sourced observations.

committee.view: Physical crude is not showing a shortage that matches a $12 Brent premium over WTI. The latest public stock path into 25 September is two builds. Aramco's November Asia official prices were cut to six-year lows. Those are offers, not a stockout.
committee.lean: No outright long. Mild lean to a narrower Brent premium, not strong enough alone.

committee.view: On-site tanker and LNG modules are the July sample and were ignored. The usable shipping line is second-hand: a Reuters tally, via The Economic Times, that Middle East exports beat pre-war levels on four of seven days late in September, even with attacks reported in the Strait of Hormuz. Mixed, and not a positionable series.
The dollar index was 102.254 against a prior close of 101.45. That is a headwind for flat-price commodities and a poor reason, by itself, to short a war market.
committee.lean: No macro hedge. Nothing is open to hedge.

committee.view: The Iran war is the dominant fact. Vessel attacks in Hormuz are reported. A Houthi claim of strikes on Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais was not confirmed by Saudi Arabia in the article. Confirmed and claimed events are not the same thing. Either can gap a stop.
committee.lean: Veto on naked shorts. No confidence upgrade for longs, because the premium is already in the price.

committee.view: Brent minus WTI at $12.18 is rare versus the last 127 sessions and ordinary versus the nine sessions since 23 September. Heating oil's crack near $102 is a regime. Henry Hub at $3.03 is not a signal. Monday product volume does not support a breakout call.
committee.lean: Spread is the only quantitative candidate, and it is a regime observation rather than an entry.

committee.view: The spread's illustrative stop at $15.50 risks $3.32 a barrel. Eight contracts would have been about 0.27% of NAV, inside the 0.25–1.0% band, with a 1.7:1 payoff to $6.50. The war can gap through that stop. A 50 score does not get to use the risk budget.
committee.lean: No trade. Cash is the risk position.

committee.view: Expected payoff is not sufficient for the tail. Opening a position to avoid a flat first week would be the failure mode this fund is built to refuse.

daily_brief.title: The Crude Oracle decision brief — 2026-10-05, week 41 inception

sections.label: Market summary
sections.text: Decision marks at 11:21 UTC: WTI Nov 26 $90.15, Brent $102.33, spread $12.18, Henry Hub Nov $3.03, dollar index 102.254. Heating-oil crack about $102. The RBOB last print was discarded.

sections.label: Brent / WTI price signal
sections.text: The spread is wide versus six months and mid-range versus the war window that started on 23 September. That distinction kept it on the watchlist at confidence 50.

sections.label: Gas / LNG signal
sections.text: Henry Hub is unchanged in any sense that matters, near $3.03. No storage figure was admitted. No LNG vessel series was fresh. No gas trade.

sections.label: Supply risk
sections.text: G7 stock-release plans are confirmed as a plan, not as a barrel count. Middle East exports were reported above pre-war levels on four of seven late-September days. Aramco cut November Asia official prices to six-year lows.

sections.label: Demand signal
sections.text: The OSP cut is the demand-side fact in hand: Asian official selling prices were lowered. It is not a global demand model.

sections.label: Inventory signal
sections.text: Secondary EIA compilations show US commercial crude at about 427.3 million barrels for the week of 25 September, after builds of 2.97 mb and 0.92 mb. The next weekly release is 7 October. EIA's own site did not answer this session.

sections.label: Geopolitical risk
sections.text: Iran war, reported Hormuz vessel attacks, and an unconfirmed claim of strikes on Aramco sites. Confirmed supply recovery and unconfirmed attacks are both in the file. Neither was promoted into a fill.

sections.label: Top opportunity today
sections.text: Short the Brent–WTI spread. Confidence 50. Illustrative entry $12.18, stop $15.50, target $6.50, about 1.7:1. Status: watch.

sections.label: Top risk today
sections.text: A Hormuz gap. Because the book is in cash, that risk does not hit NAV. The cost is missing a collapse in the premium.

sections.label: Existing positions review
sections.text: No open positions. This is inception. The retired $1,000,000 sample book is not in this NAV.

sections.label: Proposed paper trades
sections.text: None. Journal id CO-2026-W41-000 records the no-trade decision.

sections.label: Stop-loss / risk levels
sections.text: Nothing is open, so nothing can hit a stop. Illustrative stops are stored on the watchlist and were not executed.

sections.label: Cash balance
sections.text: $10,000,000. Above any cash floor because the opportunity set failed, not because a quota was filled.

sections.label: Watchlist changes
sections.text: Added: Brent–WTI spread, heating-oil crack, Brent outright, WTI outright, Henry Hub, US energy equities. No removals. No promotions.

sections.label: Bottom line
sections.text: The fund exists as of today. It has no P&L, no closed trade and no claim to have called the war. The next committee is week 42, with the 7 October EIA print in between.
